newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French 10-year bond futures settled higher on Wednesday, after short covering kicked in at a significant level at 127.64.
Traders said the market appeared to be viewing Tuesday's Fed funds quarter percent rate increase as a preventive measure.

U.S. durable goods orders rose 1.5 percent in February, compared to an upwardly revised 4.1 percent January increase, signalling continued strength in manufacturing and catching U.S. Treasuries off-guard.
But market operators are cautious ahead of next Tuesday's NAPM purchasing managers report and payrolls data on April 4.
Paris markets are closed for a long Easter weekend, with no trading on Good Friday and Easter Monday.
Traders said the June contract closed a gap opened on March 18 at 128.30 and climbed to a session high at 128.44 before retracing.
Short covering by mainly non-domestic investors took June Pibor up five basis points, drawing support from resilient U.S. Treasuries, they said.
The franc was steady at 3.3710/12 per mark versus 3.3722/27 late on Tuesday.
The market could limit itself to testing the 128.54/56 area on the June bond future, rather than run risks so close to major U.S. indicators and market holidays.

A Reuter poll of eight economists showed only one expected a Bank of France rate cut this week, in the wake of the Fed's tightening. Five of the eight thought the Bank would make small cuts in the coming months.
The gap with German rates offers the French central bank room to ease, if only to match the German repo rate in a convergence ahead of monetary union, they said.
